title: Week 32 Mastery Quiz · Public Health and Humanitarian Coordination

questions.question: The WHO Constitution describes organizational health functions. Which inference should a senior avoid?
options: Treating a constitutional mandate as proof a specific outbreak response achieved its stated outcomes.
Identifying the instrument's issuer.
Comparing official functions and actual capacity.
Studying independent public-health metrics.
questions.explanation: Treating a constitutional mandate as proof a specific outbreak response achieved its stated outcomes.

questions.question: A fictional disease bulletin reports 120 cases under a broad definition and 80 under a narrower definition. What is essential?
options: Subtract 80 and classify 40 as confirmed errors.
Reconcile definitions and testing coverage before comparing incidence trends.
Treat both case totals as the same measure.
Assume the narrower count is fabricated.
questions.explanation: Reconcile definitions and testing coverage before comparing incidence trends.

questions.question: A vaccination campaign reports 8,000 doses delivered to a district with 10,000 residents. What cannot be inferred directly?
options: That 8,000 doses arrived.
That the district has 10,000 residents.
That 80% of residents are fully vaccinated without person-level eligibility and dose-course data.
That dose counts can be recorded.
questions.explanation: That 80% of residents are fully vaccinated without person-level eligibility and dose-course data.

questions.question: Two fictional provinces have similar case counts but sharply different population sizes. What calculation helps comparison?
options: Only absolute counts.
Only the larger province's hospital number.
The number of press conferences.
Rates per a consistent population denominator and comparable ascertainment periods.
questions.explanation: Rates per a consistent population denominator and comparable ascertainment periods.

questions.question: A health authority issues a risk alert but later evidence shows the forecast overestimated severity. What builds institutional trust?
options: Transparent correction, methods disclosure, uncertainty communication and after-action review.
Delete the original alert without record.
Claim predictions are always exact.
Avoid reporting any new information.
questions.explanation: Transparent correction, methods disclosure, uncertainty communication and after-action review.

questions.question: A humanitarian convoy reaches 20 sites but a needs assessment identifies 45 inaccessible settlements. What planning issue appears?
options: Site counts prove universal reach.
Coverage bias, access barriers and service prioritization for underserved populations.
All settlements have equal needs.
The convoy destination list is an outcome evaluation.
questions.explanation: Coverage bias, access barriers and service prioritization for underserved populations.

questions.question: An epidemic simulation has a testing delay of seven days but a report compares daily confirmed cases as if they occurred that day. What bias arises?
options: Every case occurred on confirmation day.
Delays never affect curve interpretation.
Reporting lags may shift observed trends relative to infection or symptom onset dates.
Only public attitudes determine case dates.
questions.explanation: Reporting lags may shift observed trends relative to infection or symptom onset dates.

questions.question: A public-health notice appears only in one language in a multilingual region. Which equity analysis is needed?
options: One-language notices always reach everyone.
Translation necessarily reduces accuracy.
Language has no relationship to risk communication.
Assess language access, trusted dissemination channels and differential comprehension or uptake.
questions.explanation: Assess language access, trusted dissemination channels and differential comprehension or uptake.

questions.question: A fictional outbreak dashboard shows mortality counts rising while testing expands threefold. What is a careful evidence-based response?
options: Separate disease burden measures, reporting coverage, denominators and time lags before asserting one causal interpretation.
More testing necessarily causes deaths.
Every increase proves the same trend.
Case totals alone show health-system capacity.
questions.explanation: Separate disease burden measures, reporting coverage, denominators and time lags before asserting one causal interpretation.

questions.question: An aid agency claims success because expenditure met its budget but provides no service outcomes. Which evaluation is strongest?
options: Budget use automatically proves effectiveness.
Examine delivery quality, beneficiary access, health results, costs and unintended effects alongside spending.
High expenditure means equal distribution.
Service outcomes cannot be assessed.
questions.explanation: Examine delivery quality, beneficiary access, health results, costs and unintended effects alongside spending.

shortResponse: What makes collective response legitimate and effective during cross-border health and humanitarian emergencies?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
